claims.statement: The bypass fragment says enterprise administrators may block the referenced commands for Business/Enterprise license holders. It does not identify those commands in isolation; neither bypass behavior nor authorization can be inferred from the filename.

The organization-disable procedure distinguishes new billing/licensing navigation from original Copilot Access navigation and requires all policies configured before proceeding. Inspected organization-navigation includes provide UI context, not verified privileges or actual settings.

The disable procedure selects Disabled then confirms removal of seats to revoke access for all organization users, with Enterprise wording only in the ghec branch. This is a broad native/billing mutation, not a harmless diagnostic; no seats or policies changed.

The personal website settings fragment permits Pro/Pro+/Max users to allow/block public-code-matching inline suggestions, but its prompt/suggestion collection-retention choice is conditional on fpt. Those scopes cannot be extended to every edition or treated as complete information isolation.

The data-residency authentication section includes a managed-user prerequisite to update settings before sign-in. It does not define the necessary settings itself, prove SSO readiness or authorize credential changes.

The Eclipse MCP setup fragment gives two routes to configuration: chat tool configuration or preferences under Copilot MCP. Reaching a settings UI does not prove installed, authorized or safe servers.

The Eclipse prerequisite fragment requires Copilot access and Eclipse 2024-09 or newer, and requires enabled MCP servers in Copilot policy for organization/enterprise Business/Enterprise members to use MCP. A compatible editor alone is insufficient.

The editor-preview fragment requires the supplying organization or enterprise to enable Editor preview features for Business/Enterprise users. Linked policy pages and stated prerequisites are not actual target enablement receipts.
